title: Anger as enemy, understanding as friend
odia:
କ୍ରୋଧ ଠାରୁ ଶତୃ ନାହିଁ
ବୋଧ ଠାରୁ ମିତ୍ର ନାହିଁ।
literal_meaning: No enemy is greater than anger; no friend is greater than understanding.
meaning_odia: କ୍ରୋଧକୁ ବଡ଼ ଶତ୍ରୁ ଓ ବୁଝିବାର ଶକ୍ତିକୁ ବଡ଼ ମିତ୍ର ବୋଲି ଏହି କଥା ତୁଳନା କରେ। ରାଗରେ ଚାଳିତ ହେବା ବଦଳରେ କଥାକୁ ବୁଝି ବିଚାର କରିବାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି।
explanation: The two lines give inner states the roles of enemy and friend. In this editorial reading, anger can work against a person’s interests, while understanding helps them respond with judgement. The force comes from the balanced contrast.
usage_example: Before replying to an upsetting message, someone pauses to understand what happened and recalls the saying. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: କ୍ରୋଧ and ବୋଧ rhyme, while ଶତୃ and ମିତ୍ର form the opposing pair. The verse turns anger and understanding into imagined companions whose effects differ.

odia_summary: କ୍ରୋଧ ଶତ୍ରୁ ପରି, ବୁଝିବାର ଶକ୍ତି ମିତ୍ର ପରି।
english_summary: Anger is cast as an enemy and understanding as a friend.
